title: Samchan exec's testimony crucial to Romualdez plunder case -- Ombudsman spox
summary: The testimony of Felicito Guevarra, an executive of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp., could prove crucial to the Ombudsman's P7.4-billion plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez and…

blocks.text: Published November 23, 2026 6:38pm

The testimony of Felicito Guevarra, an executive of Samchan Foreign Exchange Corp., could prove crucial to the Ombudsman's P7.4-billion plunder case against former House Speaker Martin Romualdez and his co-accused, Assistant Ombudsman Mico Clavano said on Monday.

Clavano made the statement after the Ombudsman asked the Sandiganbayan to discharge Guevarra as a co-accused so he could act as a prosecution witness in Romualdez's bail hearing, replacing former Public Works Secretary Manuel Bonoan
In the same omnibus motion, the Ombudsman also asked the court to allow Guevarra to remain in the custody of the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI).
Guevarra surrendered to the NBI on Nov. 19.

Clavano said Guevarra's testimony could prove crucial to the case because, as a foreign exchange firm executive, he may provide insight into how large-scale corruption proceeds are handled in cash, often leaving little documentary or financial trail in the banking system.

“Pag ganito na kalaki 'yung nangyayaring korapsyon, usually hindi talaga dumadaan sa bangko 'yan," Clavano said during the Ombudsman's weekly radio program, TanodBayan, aired over state-run Radyo Pilipinas.
(When corruption reaches this magnitude, transactions usually do not go through banks.)
"Walang deposit slip, walang pirma, walang AMLC record na may nag-transfer ng funds from account A to account B. Usually diyan, cash na ang transactions nila,” he added.
(There are no deposit slips, signatures or Anti-Money Laundering Council records showing transfers between accounts. These transactions are usually conducted in cash.)
Guevarra could help investigators establish how cash was handled and moved, Clavano said.
He also suggested that the use of cash explained why investigators found little documentary evidence in financial records.
“Alam na ng mga public officials na hindi talaga dapat sila gumamit ng bangko kasi mahuhuli ka agad. That's all recorded. May paper trail 'yan, may pirma pa," Clavano said.
(Public officials already know they should not use banks because transactions are immediately recorded, leaving a paper trail and signatures.)
"So itong pagsuko ng isang foreign exchange [firm official], it will be substantial [to our case],” he added.
(That is why the surrender of a foreign exchange firm official would be substantial to the case.)

Clavano did not identify the transactions or individuals involved. However, the prosecution's AMLC financial investigator, Atty. Jan Mark Busa, had earlier told the Sandiganbayan that remittances worth P560.5 million to accounts linked to Romualdez from 2022 to 2025 were not related to flood control projects.
Clavano stressed that the Ombudsman had never claimed that the alleged proceeds of corruption were transferred directly to Romualdez through bank accounts reflected in AMLC records.

“Wala naman talagang dadaan sa account. Hindi naman talaga 'yan ang theory ng Ombudsman. Ngayon, sumuko na 'yung sa money exchange [firm executive], dito natin malalaman kung ano talaga ang nangyari,” he said.

(Those transactions would not actually pass through bank accounts. That has never been the Ombudsman's theory. Now that the money exchange firm executive has surrendered, this is where we will find out what really happened.)

Meanwhile, Romualdez's lawyer, Judd Roy III, questioned the prosecution's move to replace Bonoan as a witness, saying the defense had prepared its strategy based on the original set of prosecution witnesses and the criminal information filed against his client.

“The lines of defense were prepared, evidentiary positions were taken… even our cross-examination of the other witnesses was all in recognition of that [criminal] information [filed]. And now they're saying that it will not substantially affect the case," Roy said in a separate interview.
"Put yourself in our shoes. Do you honestly believe that is the case?” he added.— MCG, GMA News
